sections.overview: Rhopalura granosa is a little-known orthonectid, a microscopic marine parasite.
sections.identification: Orthonectids have a highly simplified body plan; the genus is distinguished from related genera by microscopic anatomical characters.
sections.habitat: Published records place this species in a marine bivalve host in the eastern North Atlantic.
sections.diet: It is parasitic in the bivalve Heteranomia squamula, identified as its host in the original description.
sections.behavior: The original species paper includes observations of swimming, but the available account is brief.
sections.reproduction: The references consulted do not provide a concise species-specific account of reproduction.
sections.ecology: Unlike R. ophiocomae, which is reported from brittle stars, R. granosa is known from a bivalve host.
sections.conservation: No conservation assessment for this microscopic parasite was found in the sources consulted.
